Because x(0)=1 and z(0)=0, the initial mismatch drives dz/dt>0 immediately; thus z should rise from zero before later relaxing with the motion.

The motion should be dissipative overall: oscillation amplitudes in x and v decay over time due to linear and nonlinear drag, though not necessarily monotonically cycle-to-cycle because of internal lag.
Nonlinear drag is weak near v≈0 and stronger at larger |v|, so deceleration magnitude should increase faster than linearly with speed during faster portions of the trajectory.

The restoring term is near parent-like for small |z| but shows reduced hardening relative to an unsaturated cubic law once saturation_strain_coefficient*z^2 becomes appreciable; turning-point restoring acceleration should therefore grow sub-cubically with larger attained |z| within the trajectory.

Because z is lagged and c evolves, identical x values reached on different parts of the transient need not produce identical dv_dt; a looped acceleration/displacement relation is expected rather than a single instantaneous elastic curve.

rationale: The provided typed ODE contract is preserved exactly as required: target state v, single time axis t, and the inherited 4-state system with fixed initial conditions. Structural analysis of the target expression alone looks explicit in v and z, but the record includes an explicit ODE-system contract with additional governed states x, z, c; per the contract instructions this system-level typing must be kept. Parameter values are chosen to keep the dynamics finite and passive while making the intended distinctions visible in one transient relaxation experiment starting from the inherited nonzero displacement. With mass=1 and spring_constant=12, the nominal small-strain oscillation timescale is comparable to a period around 1.8, so t in [0,20] captures several cycles and decay. relaxation_time=0.7 is neither very fast nor frozen relative to the oscillation, so z visibly lags x. conditioning_rate=0.9 and conditioning_strain_coefficient=0.6 make c evolve on a comparable transient timescale and modulate the z-relaxation rate without risking sign reversal in 1+conditioning_strain_coefficient*c. cubic_stiffness_coefficient=1.5 gives noticeable moderate-strain hardening when |z| reaches order 1, while saturation_strain_coefficient=0.8 is positive and comparable but smaller-order than that stiffening scale, so the effective cubic correction bends over for moderate |z| instead of remaining purely Duffing-like; this avoids placing the whole trajectory either in the parent-recovery limit or deep saturation. damping_coefficient=0.8 plus nonlinear_drag_coefficient=0.25 yields clear dissipation, with nonlinear drag weak near rest and more visible during faster mid-cycle motion. The inherited initial condition x(0)=1, z(0)=0 creates an immediate relaxation mismatch x-z=1 that activates the internal-memory mechanism without altering the contract. Exact input-output pairs should therefore be generated by integrating the full inherited system over time and reading out the target state v together with its target-state RHS.

scenario_text: A one-dimensional mass is attached to an elastic support and experiences a linear resistance proportional to its velocity. Its displacement and velocity evolve from independently chosen initial conditions while the restoring and resistive mechanisms act continuously. The target is the instantaneous acceleration, with parameters fixed in the baseline experiment.

response_change.parent_relation: The target mapping is affine in the observed states: dv_dt = -(spring_constant/mass) * x - (damping_coefficient/mass) * v, so the restoring slope with respect to x is one constant value for all amplitudes.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the full-range linear-support assumption so the restoring contribution depends nonlinearly on displacement, giving an amplitude-dependent restoring slope while preserving odd symmetry under x -> -x.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories with different initial displacement amplitudes but the same mass and damping, larger |x| produces stronger curvature in dv_dt versus x than the parent's single linear slope can match with one shared parameter set.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when the motion explores displacements large enough that support nonlinearity is not negligible compared with the linear term, while damping remains passive and no external drive is present.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate amplitudes may show small but systematic deviation from a single dv_dt-versus-x slope; in holdout, larger-amplitude trajectories extend the same amplitude-dependent curvature rather than introducing a new mechanism.
plan.continuation_path: In the small-displacement limit, or when the nonlinear correction coefficient tends to zero, the model reduces continuously to the parent damped linear oscillator.
plan.gap_statement: The support is assumed exactly linear over the full displacement range, omitting amplitude-dependent restoring stiffness that is common once deflections are no longer infinitesimal.
plan.baseline_assumption: The support response is linear over the full displacement range.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Non-Hookean elastic restoring behavior of the support at finite displacement, such as a Duffing-type cubic stiffness correction.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the idealized full-range Hooke-law assumption rather than add an unrelated process. The parent says that at fixed mass and damping, changing initial displacement only scales the sampled x values along one line in the dv_dt-versus-(x,v) relation; the restoring slope with respect to x is constant. The child would make that slope depend on amplitude, so when comparing trajectories started with small versus larger displacement but similar velocity range, the acceleration becomes disproportionately more restoring at larger |x|. With one shared parent parameter set, the linear model cannot fit both the near-origin slope and the stronger outer restoring curvature simultaneously. This changes the scored target mapping directly because dv_dt as a function of observed x and v is altered, not merely an auxiliary trajectory. The effect is admissible in passive one-dimensional motion, preserves continuity and sign-reversal symmetry, and remains energy-dissipative because the damping law is unchanged and no drive is introduced. The limitation is that if all observed displacements stay very small, the refinement is practically unidentifiable and the parent is recovered.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when the experiment includes a spread of velocity magnitudes such that inertial or elastic motion produces both small-|v| intervals and finite-speed intervals where additional drag curvature is not negligible; near |v|≈0 the child should reduce to the parent within measurement resolution.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate speeds already show slight excess damping relative to the linear law; in holdout, larger speeds extend the same monotone curvature so the mismatch of any single refitted linear damping coefficient becomes clearer.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the low-speed limit or by setting the nonlinear drag strength to zero.
plan.gap_statement: The model treats resistance as exactly proportional to velocity over the full accessible speed range, omitting the common finite-speed departure from Stokes-like drag.
plan.baseline_assumption: The resistance is smooth and depends only on instantaneous velocity.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Velocity-dependent resistance remains dissipative and odd under velocity reversal but acquires nonlinear speed dependence from fluid/air drag or internal friction beyond the strictly linear regime.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's full-range linear-damping assumption while keeping the same states and symmetry constraints. The parent target mapping from observed states to dv_dt is the sum of the existing elastic term and a resistive term with one fixed slope in v. Varying initial conditions already changes the visited velocity range under the current observation protocol, so this mechanism can be activated without adding inputs or hidden states. Hold mass, spring_constant, damping_coefficient, and cubic_stiffness_coefficient fixed, and compare portions of trajectories with small versus larger |v|: the parent predicts the same incremental damping per unit velocity everywhere, whereas the child predicts stronger deceleration at larger speeds and near-parent behavior close to rest. This is a genuine target-mapping change, not merely an auxiliary-trajectory change, because dv_dt at the same x but different |v| departs from an affine dependence on v. The refinement is scientifically admissible provided the explored speed range is large enough that nonlinear drag is measurable but not so extreme that other omitted effects dominate. If all observed speeds are very small, the contrast may be weak and the parent remains an adequate approximation.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when the support relaxation time is comparable to the oscillation time scale, so deformation changes appreciably before the support fully re-equilibrates; strongest for moderate-to-large amplitudes where elastic loading is appreciable and for transients or frequencies not asymptotically slow.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within training trajectories from varying initial conditions, slow passages near turning points and faster crossings near the origin sample different deformation rates; in holdout, larger-amplitude or more weakly damped trajectories extend this same rate-dependent elastic lag, enlarging the hysteresis without changing the mechanism.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the fast-relaxation limit where the internal support state tracks displacement quasi-instantly, or equivalently when the relaxation effect strength tends to zero.
plan.promotion_reason: A genuinely history-dependent restoring response cannot be represented by refitting fixed coefficients in an instantaneous function of x and v alone; one internal state is needed to encode delayed support equilibration while preserving continuity and passive dynamics.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes the elastic support responds instantaneously to displacement, omitting viscoelastic relaxation of the support itself.
plan.baseline_assumption: The support response is an instantaneous function of current displacement with fixed properties and no internal memory.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Standard linear solid/anelastic support relaxation: part of the elastic load is carried by an internal strain-like degree of freedom that relaxes toward the current displacement over finite time, creating passive rate-dependent stiffness.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the instantaneous-support assumption rather than add another velocity drag term. Vary initial conditions to obtain trajectories with different characteristic speeds and amplitudes while holding mass, spring_constant, damping_coefficient, cubic_stiffness_coefficient, and nonlinear_drag_coefficient fixed. In the parent, once x and v are specified, dv_dt is fully determined; any acceleration-versus-displacement curvature is fixed apart from the explicit odd damping shift in v. In the child, the same x and v can yield different dv_dt depending on whether the support's internal deformation has caught up, producing a measurable hysteretic curvature change in the target mapping itself, not merely in an auxiliary variable. This is scientifically admissible for polymeric, rubber, foam, or internally damped supports when relaxation time is not negligible relative to the oscillation period. A single refit of the parent parameters cannot reproduce both near-quasi-static elastic response and lagged dynamic stiffness across these conditions because the parent has no memory channel: it maps identical instantaneous observables x and v to identical dv_dt, whereas the child does not. Limitation: if relaxation is either extremely fast or extremely slow over the entire observed window, the added state may collapse effectively to the parent or to a nearly constant bias-free elastic branch, reducing observability.

contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate amplitudes already reveal some amplitude dependence of lag; in holdout, larger but still admissible excursions strengthen the same deformation-dependent relaxation effect rather than introducing a different mechanism.
contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the relaxation rate is deformation-independent, e.g. the coefficient of strain dependence tends to zero.
contract.promotion_reason: A realistic strain-dependent relaxation law is often implemented through an internal configurational state controlling support conditioning or anelastic saturation; existing x, v, and z do not separately encode this evolving internal phase, so one additional state is the natural minimal freedom if the refinement is written mechanistically rather than as an ad hoc coefficient tweak.
contract.scientific_mechanism: Passive amplitude-dependent anelastic relaxation or conditioning of the support, causing the internal load-transfer kinetics to change with deformation state while remaining dissipative and sign-symmetric.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because the relaxation coefficient of the existing z process now depends on a history-carrying internal state c, creating amplitude-dependent phase evolution and hysteresis rather than a single globally refittable lag constant.
contract.assumption_before: The support relaxation toward displacement occurs with a constant linear timescale independent of deformation history and strain level.
contract.assumption_after: The support relaxation coefficient depends on an evolving conditioning state driven by deformation magnitude, so the relaxation phase is amplitude dependent.
contract.before_fragment: -((spring_constant * (1 + cubic_stiffness_coefficient * z**2)) / mass) * z - (damping_coefficient / mass) * v - (nonlinear_drag_coefficient / mass) * Abs(v) * v
contract.after_fragment: -((spring_constant * (1 + cubic_stiffness_coefficient * z**2)) / mass) * z - (damping_coefficient / mass) * v - (nonlinear_drag_coefficient / mass) * Abs(v) * v
contract.observable_signature: Relative to the parent's one-phase lag law, the child predicts that when mass, damping, and spring parameters are held fixed and trajectory amplitude increases within the admissible range, the acceleration-versus-z relationship changes curvature and phase because z evolves faster or slower according to the conditioning state c. This is a changed target mapping through state coupling, not merely an auxiliary-state modification, because dv_dt uses z and the z trajectory is systematically reshaped by c under the same observation protocol.
contract.shortcut_blocked: Refitting one parent relaxation_time can only impose one amplitude-blind lag character across all trajectories. It may match either small-excursion or large-excursion loop curvature, but not both when conditioning makes the z update coefficient vary during motion with deformation history. The child therefore cannot be absorbed by a single shared parent parameter set except in the weak-activation limit where conditioning_strain_coefficient is negligible.

range_suggestions.c: nonnegative internal conditioning level; typically 0 to order(x**2) over admissible motions
range_suggestions.conditioning_rate: positive and comparable to, slower than, or faster than 1/relaxation_time to span weak to strong conditioning memory
range_suggestions.conditioning_strain_coefficient: nonnegative and small-to-moderate so 1 + conditioning_strain_coefficient*c stays positive over admissible trajectories

response_change.parent_relation: The restoring contribution to dv_dt is odd in z with a fixed cubic stiffening factor, so after conditioning states are fixed the elastic slope-versus-deformation relation is determined by one shared monotone cubic law.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the purely cubic amplitude dependence of the restoring law with a saturating odd nonlinearity in deformation, so the incremental restoring slope initially follows the parent-like small-strain law but bends over at larger |z| instead of growing indefinitely.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories that reach small versus moderate-to-large internal deformation |z|, the child predicts weaker-than-cubic growth of peak restoring acceleration at large amplitude, giving reduced hardening of turning-point acceleration compared with the parent.

plan.activation_condition: Visible when trajectories explore a regime with |cubic_stiffness_coefficient*z**2| not small compared with 1, so the parent's cubic hardening would materially change acceleration; weakly visible in the small-deformation limit.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, modest amplitudes show only slight deviation from linear stiffness; in holdout, larger admissible amplitudes extend the same trend and reveal that restoring acceleration grows sub-cubically rather than continuing the parent's fixed cubic hardening.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the saturation scale to infinity or, equivalently, restricting to sufficiently small |z| where the refined restoring law has the same leading linear-plus-cubic expansion.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes the finite-amplitude support nonlinearity is well represented over the full admissible deformation range by one polynomial cubic correction with no saturation of incremental stiffness.
plan.baseline_assumption: The support response is linear over the full displacement range.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Geometric/material stiffening that is Duffing-like at moderate strain but softens relative to a pure cubic extrapolation as fibers, linkage geometry, or local compliance redistribution approach a finite reconfiguration range while remaining passive and odd under sign reversal.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's fixed cubic hardening assumption rather than add a new process. The parent target mapping from observed states to acceleration contains a single deformation gain curve: for fixed v, c, and x through z, dv_dt depends on z through one odd polynomial restoring law whose curvature is locked by one shared cubic coefficient. Varying initial displacement while holding parameters fixed changes the explored |z| range, but the parent necessarily predicts that peak restoring acceleration continues to steepen with z according to that same cubic trend. A child with a saturating odd stiffness law changes the target mapping itself, not only auxiliary trajectories, because dv_dt at the same supplied z and v differs systematically: near z=0 it matches the parent asymptotically, while at larger |z| its slope and curvature bend over. This is observable when admissible motions drive the internal deformation into moderate strain, especially near turning points where v is small and the elastic term dominates acceleration. One shared refit of the parent parameters cannot generally reproduce both the small-amplitude near-Duffing behavior and the reduced large-amplitude hardening, because increasing or decreasing the cubic coefficient changes curvature globally rather than producing the child’s crossover from cubic-like growth to saturation. Limitation: if all sampled trajectories stay in the infinitesimal-strain regime, the refinement is practically unidentifiable and the parent is recovered.

contract.assumption_before: The support response uses one unsaturating cubic stiffening law across the admissible deformation range.
contract.assumption_after: The support stiffening coefficient depends on deformation and saturates at larger |z|, preserving odd passive elasticity but limiting further hardening.
contract.before_fragment: -((spring_constant * (1 + cubic_stiffness_coefficient * z**2)) / mass) * z - (damping_coefficient / mass) * v - (nonlinear_drag_coefficient / mass) * Abs(v) * v

baseline_assumptions: The support response is linear over the full displacement range.
The resistance is smooth and depends only on instantaneous velocity.
Motion is constrained to one spatial dimension.
The support and mass have fixed properties and do not undergo structural deformation.
scientific_constraints: Mechanical energy cannot increase when the resistive coefficient is positive and no external drive is applied.
The displacement and velocity must be continuous in time.
The acceleration must reverse appropriately under simultaneous sign reversal of displacement and velocity.
refinement_agenda: Add a nonlinear restoring response at large displacement.
Add dry-contact resistance with direction-dependent behavior.
Allow the support properties to vary with displacement.

response_change.parent_relation: The target mapping is affine in the observed states: dv_dt = -(spring_constant/mass) * x - (damping_coefficient/mass) * v, so the restoring slope with respect to x is one constant value for all amplitudes.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the full-range linear-support assumption so the restoring contribution depends nonlinearly on displacement, giving an amplitude-dependent restoring slope while preserving odd symmetry under x -> -x.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories with different initial displacement amplitudes but the same mass and damping, larger |x| produces stronger curvature in dv_dt versus x than the parent's single linear slope can match with one shared parameter set.

evolution_contracts.activation_condition: Observable when the motion explores displacements large enough that support nonlinearity is not negligible compared with the linear term, while damping remains passive and no external drive is present.
evolution_contracts.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate amplitudes may show small but systematic deviation from a single dv_dt-versus-x slope; in holdout, larger-amplitude trajectories extend the same amplitude-dependent curvature rather than introducing a new mechanism.
evolution_contracts.continuation_path: In the small-displacement limit, or when the nonlinear correction coefficient tends to zero, the model reduces continuously to the parent damped linear oscillator.
evolution_contracts.domain_mechanism: Amplitude-dependent elastic stiffness in a passive support
evolution_contracts.scientific_mechanism: Non-Hookean elastic restoring behavior of the support at finite displacement, such as a Duffing-type cubic stiffness correction.
evolution_contracts.difficulty_rationale: The refinement is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because the effective restoring gain now depends on the state through 1 + cubic_stiffness_coefficient * x**2, so one must capture state-dependent curvature rather than retune one constant slope.
evolution_contracts.assumption_before: The support response is linear over the full displacement range.
evolution_contracts.assumption_after: The support has amplitude-dependent stiffness, modeled by a cubic Duffing-type correction to the restoring law.
evolution_contracts.after_fragment: -((spring_constant * (1 + cubic_stiffness_coefficient * x**2)) / mass) * x - (damping_coefficient / mass) * v
evolution_contracts.parent_reduction: For cubic_stiffness_coefficient = 0, or in the regime cubic_stiffness_coefficient * x**2 << 1, the child collapses to the parent expression.
evolution_contracts.observable_signature: Holding mass and damping fixed, compare trajectories started from different displacement amplitudes under the same observation protocol: near x = 0 the dv_dt-versus-x relation approaches the parent's linear slope, but at larger |x| the child shows stronger odd-symmetric restoring curvature due to the x**3 contribution. This is a changed target mapping, not merely an auxiliary trajectory change, because dv_dt computed from the observed states (x,v) is directly altered.
evolution_contracts.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set only provides one x-slope coefficient spring_constant/mass for all amplitudes, so it cannot simultaneously match the near-origin linear behavior and the stronger outer restoring acceleration seen when |x| is larger. Refitting spring_constant and damping_coefficient across all data can shift the global line but cannot create the required state-dependent curvature in dv_dt as a function of observed x and v.

response_change.parent_relation: The resistive contribution to acceleration is a single linear gain of velocity, -(damping_coefficient/mass)*v, so at fixed x the target depends affinely on v with constant slope independent of speed.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the idealized linear resistance with amplitude-dependent drag that remains odd in v but grows more strongly at larger |v|, so at fixed x the target-versus-v curve bends and its effective damping slope increases with speed.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories started with different initial speeds while mass, spring_constant, and cubic_stiffness_coefficient are held fixed, large-|v| segments decay faster than a single linear damping law predicts, while near v≈0 the response approaches the parent law.

evolution_contracts.activation_condition: Observable when the experiment includes a spread of velocity magnitudes such that inertial or elastic motion produces both small-|v| intervals and finite-speed intervals where additional drag curvature is not negligible; near |v|≈0 the child should reduce to the parent within measurement resolution.
evolution_contracts.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate speeds already show slight excess damping relative to the linear law; in holdout, larger speeds extend the same monotone curvature so the mismatch of any single refitted linear damping coefficient becomes clearer.
evolution_contracts.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the low-speed limit or by setting the nonlinear drag strength to zero.
evolution_contracts.scientific_mechanism: Velocity-dependent resistance remains dissipative and odd under velocity reversal but acquires nonlinear speed dependence from fluid/air drag or internal friction beyond the strictly linear regime.
evolution_contracts.difficulty_rationale: This embedding is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the resistive load depends jointly on the state magnitude and the drag parameter through Abs(v)*v, creating speed-dependent curvature in the target mapping rather than a single globally refittable slope.
evolution_contracts.assumption_before: The resistance is smooth and depends only on instantaneous velocity through a strictly linear law.
evolution_contracts.assumption_after: The resistance still depends only on instantaneous velocity and remains odd under velocity reversal, but includes a finite-speed nonlinear drag contribution.
evolution_contracts.before_fragment: -((spring_constant * (1 + cubic_stiffness_coefficient * x**2)) / mass) * x - (damping_coefficient / mass) * v
evolution_contracts.after_fragment: -((spring_constant * (1 + cubic_stiffness_coefficient * x**2)) / mass) * x - (damping_coefficient / mass) * v - (nonlinear_drag_coefficient / mass) * Abs(v) * v
evolution_contracts.parent_reduction: Set nonlinear_drag_coefficient to zero, or remain in the regime where nonlinear_drag_coefficient*Abs(v) << damping_coefficient.
evolution_contracts.observable_signature: At fixed x, plotting dv_dt plus the elastic contribution against v gives a straight line in the parent but an odd curve with increasing magnitude of slope as |v| grows in the child. This is observable along trajectories that traverse both low-speed and moderate-speed segments under the same fixed parameter set.
evolution_contracts.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of damping_coefficient can match either the near-zero slope or the stronger high-speed dissipation, but not both simultaneously across conditions with different visited speed ranges, because the parent remains affine in v whereas the child adds the non-affine term Abs(v)*v.

response_change.parent_relation: The restoring force is an instantaneous odd function of displacement only: for fixed parameters, dv_dt versus x at a given v has a single time-invariant cubic-shaped curve.
response_change.child_relation: The restoring force retains odd symmetry in x but its effective stiffness evolves during motion because the support relaxes internally, so dv_dt versus x at a given v depends on the recent deformation history through a lagged internal state.
response_change.observable_effect: At the same instantaneous x and v reached on different parts of the trajectory, the acceleration differs because the support has not fully equilibrated; this appears as rate-dependent hysteresis/looping in the acceleration-versus-displacement relation and amplitude-dependent phase lag beyond what velocity damping alone produces.

evolution_contracts.activation_condition: Observable when the support relaxation time is comparable to the oscillation time scale, so deformation changes appreciably before the support fully re-equilibrates; strongest for moderate-to-large amplitudes where elastic loading is appreciable and for transients or frequencies not asymptotically slow.
evolution_contracts.train_hidden_contrast: Within training trajectories from varying initial conditions, slow passages near turning points and faster crossings near the origin sample different deformation rates; in holdout, larger-amplitude or more weakly damped trajectories extend this same rate-dependent elastic lag, enlarging the hysteresis without changing the mechanism.
evolution_contracts.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the fast-relaxation limit where the internal support state tracks displacement quasi-instantly, or equivalently when the relaxation effect strength tends to zero.
evolution_contracts.promotion_reason: A genuinely history-dependent restoring response cannot be represented by refitting fixed coefficients in an instantaneous function of x and v alone; one internal state is needed to encode delayed support equilibration while preserving continuity and passive dynamics.
evolution_contracts.domain_mechanism: anelastic support relaxation with finite strain-memory capacity
evolution_contracts.scientific_mechanism: Standard linear solid/anelastic support relaxation: part of the elastic load is carried by an internal strain-like degree of freedom that relaxes toward the current displacement over finite time, creating passive rate-dependent stiffness.
evolution_contracts.difficulty_rationale: This embedding is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the target law now depends on a bounded lag state that filters displacement changes over a finite timescale, so identical instantaneous x and v need not imply identical dv_dt. The relaxation channel acts like a finite-capacity memory response: when motion is slow z nearly tracks x, while at faster deformation rates z lags and the effective restoring branch bends away from the parent curve.
evolution_contracts.assumption_before: The support response is an instantaneous function of current displacement with fixed properties and no internal memory.
evolution_contracts.assumption_after: The support load is carried by an internal deformation variable that relaxes toward displacement over finite time before entering the nonlinear restoring law.
evolution_contracts.before_fragment: -((spring_constant * (1 + cubic_stiffness_coefficient * x**2)) / mass) * x - (damping_coefficient / mass) * v - (nonlinear_drag_coefficient / mass) * Abs(v) * v
evolution_contracts.after_fragment: -((spring_constant * (1 + cubic_stiffness_coefficient * z**2)) / mass) * z - (damping_coefficient / mass) * v - (nonlinear_drag_coefficient / mass) * Abs(v) * v
evolution_contracts.parent_reduction: In the fast-relaxation limit relaxation_time -> 0, z -> x and the full target equation becomes the parent expression.
evolution_contracts.observable_signature: Compared at fixed parameters across trajectories generated by different initial conditions, the parent predicts one unique dv_dt for each instantaneous pair (x, v). The child predicts looped acceleration-versus-displacement curves because z lags x when relaxation_time is comparable to the oscillation timescale; thus the same x and v can yield different dv_dt on different trajectory segments, with the contrast strongest at moderate-to-large elastic loading and diminishing in the quasi-static limit.
evolution_contracts.shortcut_blocked: Refitting all parent coefficients still leaves an instantaneous mapping dv_dt=f(x,v) with no memory channel, so one shared parent parameter set cannot reproduce observations where identical sampled x and v correspond to different accelerations due to different z histories. The discrepancy is structural, not a matter of retuning stiffness or damping magnitudes, because the child adds path dependence in the scored target itself.

response_change.parent_relation: The delayed support force depends on the internal deformation z through a memoryless odd polynomial spring law, so at fixed z and parameters the target mapping dv_dt(z,v) has a single cubic-amplitude elastic curvature independent of how rapidly the deformation is being updated.
response_change.child_relation: Keep the same delayed elastic branch but relax the assumption that the support relaxation rate is constant: make relaxation progressively strain-dependent so the effective restoring contribution to dv_dt changes with both deformation magnitude and relaxation state, producing amplitude-dependent hysteretic curvature in the target mapping through z dynamics.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories with the same initial displacement scale but different attained deformation amplitudes, the acceleration-versus-z loop changes shape: larger excursions show a different lag-induced restoring curvature and phase delay than small excursions, not reproducible by one parent parameter set with fixed relaxation_time.
